\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Finite Law}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomVariables.FiniteLaw
\section{Overview}
Finite-support random variables have weighted-sum integral and norm formulas on arbitrary finite measure spaces. Two-point laws yield explicit centered moments and atom weights.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Integral under a finite law]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_law_integral}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a finite measure space, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable,
and let $s\subseteq\mathbb R$ be finite, with $X\in s$ almost everywhere. For every
function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $\int f(X)\,d\mu=\sum_{x\in s}\mu(X=x)f(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Affine norm for a finite law]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_law_affine_norm_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_law_integral, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.HasAtomLowerBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.HasAtomLowerBound.memLp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm_rpow}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a finite measure space, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable,
and let $s\subseteq\mathbb R$ be finite, with $X\in s$ almost everywhere. For $q>0$ and
$a,b\in\mathbb R$, the real-valued random-variable norm satisfies
$N_q(a+bX)^2=\left(\sum_{x\in s}\mu(X=x)\,|a+bx|^q\right)^{2/q}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Almost-sure support on two points]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.ae_two_point_of_mass_sum}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, and
let $x,y\in\mathbb R$ be distinct. If $\mu(X=x)+\mu(X=y)=1$, then $X$ belongs to
$\{x,y\}$ almost surely.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Affine norm for a two-point law]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.two_point_affine_norm_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.ae_two_point_of_mass_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_law_affine_norm_sq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, and
let $x,y,\lambda\in\mathbb R$ with $x\ne y$ and $0\le\lambda\le1$. Suppose
$\mu(X=x)=\lambda$ and $\mu(X=y)=1-\lambda$. For $q>0$ and $a,b\in\mathbb R$,
$N_q(a+bX)^2=\left(\lambda|a+bx|^q+(1-\lambda)|a+by|^q\right)^{2/q}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Moments of a centered two-point law]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.centered_two_point_moments}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.ae_two_point_of_mass_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_law_integral, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.two_point_affine_norm_sq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, and
let $0\le\lambda\le1$. Suppose $\mu(X=1-\lambda)=\lambda$ and
$\mu(X=-\lambda)=1-\lambda$. Then $\int X\,d\mu=0$, and the square of the real-valued
random-variable norm at exponent $2$ is $N_2(X)^2=\lambda(1-\lambda)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Weights of atoms in a finite probability law]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_probability_atom_weights}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_law_integral}
\difficulty{3}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, and
let $s\subseteq\mathbb R$ be finite, with $X\in s$ almost everywhere. If $\lambda\ge0$
and $\mu(X=x)\ge\lambda$ for every $x\in s$, then the real atom weights sum to one,
$\sum_{x\in s}\mu(X=x)=1$, and each satisfies $\mu(X=x)\ge\lambda$.
\end{theorem}
